headline: Habagat Keeps Rain Risk Over Western and Northern Luzon After Tuesday Warnings
seoTitle: Habagat Rain Risk Continues Over Western, Northern Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA continued to monitor Habagat-driven rain over parts of Luzon into August 26 after Tuesday rainfall warnings affected Zambales and parts of Bataan.
deck: Tuesday's Yellow rainfall warning covered Zambales and parts of Bataan, while PAGASA's early-Wednesday advisories continued to flag monsoon rain across northern Luzon.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Southwest Monsoon continued to influence Luzon into Wednesday after PAGASA placed Zambales and parts of Bataan under a Yellow rainfall warning on Tuesday, August 25.

The Tuesday warning covered Zambales and the Bataan municipalities of Dinalupihan, Hermosa and Morong, where flooding was possible in flood-prone areas. Other parts of Central Luzon and Metro Manila were also monitored for lighter to occasionally heavy rain during the day.

sections.heading: Early Wednesday outlook
paragraphs: PAGASA's Northern Luzon regional advisory issued at 2:00 AM on August 26 continued to forecast light to moderate, at times heavy rain over parts of Batanes, Cagayan, La Union, Benguet, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur and Pangasinan.
The public and local disaster offices were advised to continue monitoring conditions, particularly in communities vulnerable to flash floods and landslides.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The approved FMB News brief said heavy-rainfall advisories for Metro Manila had been terminated late Tuesday as the monsoon rainband shifted west. FMB News could independently confirm the Tuesday Zambales-Bataan warning and the continuing early-Wednesday northern Luzon advisories, but not a retrievable NCR termination bulletin carrying all of the brief's claimed details.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Rainfall advisories can change within hours. Residents in western and northern Luzon should rely on the latest PAGASA regional warnings and local disaster-office instructions rather than older warning maps.
